title: Call Stability Protocol: SLO-aware Backoff, Idempotency, and Multi-region Failover Guidelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define and standardize a Call Stability Protocol (CSP) across services and SDKs that unifies SLO-driven retry/timeout/backoff behavior, hedged request semantics, idempotency key handling, circuit breaker integration, and controlled load-shedding for multi-region failover scenarios. This ticket produces a consumable spec and SDK reference implementation for Go, Python, and TypeScript clients plus runtime hooks for the serving layer.
acceptance_criteria: Published CSP spec doc that maps SLO classes (P0/P1) to concrete retry/timeouts/backoff parameters for sync and streaming calls
SDK reference implementations (Go/Python/TS) expose consistent primitives: CallContext(SLO), IdempotencyKey, HedgePolicy, and CircuitBreakerHints
Runtime integration tests demonstrating graceful multi-region failover with bounded extra cost (hedging limits) and preserved exactly-once semantics for idempotent write paths
Console dashboards show per-route policy adherence and incidents where load-shedding or fallback occurred
Migration plan for server and client libraries with clear toggles and rollout checklist
notes: SLO classes: define three SLO bands (Express: p99<=50ms, Interactive: p99<=200ms, Batch: p99<=2s). Each band maps to default timeout, per-call retry budget, and max hedged clones.

Idempotency semantics: canonical header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key' is preferred. Keys are required for non-read RPCs when retries or hedges are enabled. Server MUST return 409 with diagnostics if duplicate non-idempotent call detected and idempotency header missing.

Hedged requests: defaults limited to 1 hedged clone for Express/Interactive; Batch: hedging disabled by default. Hedge jitter must be randomized in [20ms, 80ms] for Express to avoid synchronized spikes.

Circuit breakers: per-route token-bucket-based breaker with sliding window error-rate and latency thresholds. Breaker exposes 'soft' and 'hard' tripping: soft triggers reduce concurrency and enable load-shedding, hard trips fail fast to upstream fallback routes.
Load-shedding policy: runtime exposes a prioritized queue and per-tenant shedding where requests with lower priority SLOs are rejected early with Retry-After and structured diagnostic payload.

Multi-region failover: prefer synchronous fanout to multiple regions only for read-only requests. For writes, prefer single-region primary with async replication; on primary outage, use leader-election flow and require explicit idempotency key replay with causal tokens.
Costs: hedged requests increase per-token cost; spec includes a cost-governor tied to customer tier and route to bound hedging spend.
Observability: include tracing tags 'rw.slo_class', 'rw.hedge_count', 'rw.idempotency_key' and metrics for hedged_latency_reduction and hedged_extra_tokens_consumed.

Compatibility: SDK default behavior must be conservative and opt-in for aggressive hedging. A feature flag 'csp.enable_experimental_hedges' will gate early rollouts. Backwards-compatible headers supported for older runtimes.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, SDK, and Console leads. Agreed on three SLO bands and requirement for a single canonical idempotency header.
2026-02-22: Prototype hedged client implemented in Go (internal branch). Basic hedge jitter and cancellation propagation works across gRPC and HTTP paths.
2026-03-01: Design review: PM requested stronger guardrails on hedges due to cost concerns. Decision: add cost-governor and per-org hedging caps.

2026-03-05: Security review requested for idempotency key storage and replay window. Follow-up: use bounded in-memory cache with optional encrypted persistent store behind KMS for long replay windows.
2026-03-09: Integration test plan added: chaos experiments for region partition, simulated slow tail latencies, and breaker hysteresis tuning. Assigned to SRE test squad.
